subject: Social Science
central_question: How do minerals and energy resources occur, support development and require careful conservation?
in_scope_units: Meaning, uses and classification of minerals.
Mode of occurrence of minerals in veins, lodes, beds, layers, residual deposits, placers and ocean water.
Distribution and uses of ferrous, non-ferrous, non-metallic and rock minerals in India.
Hazards of mining and conservation of finite mineral resources.
Conventional energy resources: coal, petroleum, natural gas and electricity.
Non-conventional energy resources: atomic, solar, wind, biogas, tidal and geothermal energy.
Conservation of energy resources and sustainable energy choices.
banned_topics: Detailed manufacturing processes and industrial location from Manufacturing Industries.
Detailed rock cycle and landform processes beyond the mineral occurrences stated in this chapter.
Detailed dam debates from Water Resources.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every mineral occurrence is an economically usable ore.
known_pitfalls.correction: An ore must contain a mineral in sufficient concentration for extraction to be commercially viable.

known_pitfalls.claim: Bauxite is deposited in veins and lodes.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter states that bauxite forms as a residual mass after decomposition and removal of soluble material from surface rocks.

known_pitfalls.claim: Hydel and thermal electricity are both renewable.
known_pitfalls.correction: Hydel electricity uses renewable flowing water, while thermal power uses non-renewable coal, petroleum or natural gas.

known_pitfalls.claim: Conservation means stopping all mineral extraction.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter recommends planned use, improved technology for low-grade ores, recycling, scrap use and substitutes.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 2(ii) to define a mineral precisely.
Use NCERT Exercise 1(i) to identify bauxite as a residual mineral deposit.
Use NCERT Exercise 2(iv) to explain why minerals must be conserved.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(i) to organise the distribution of coal in India.
Use NCERT Exercise 3(ii) to explain why solar energy has a bright future in India.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with “EXERCISES”, Questions 1 to 3, followed by a mineral crossword activity.
